title: The space in the pot
iast: ātmā hy ākāśavaj jīvair ghaṭākāśair ivoditaḥ
ghaṭādivac ca saṃghātair jātāv etan nidarśanam
english: The Self is like space. It is spoken of as many individual selves, as space is spoken of as the spaces inside pots, and bodies are like the pots. This is the example for being born.
When the pots are broken, the space that was in them is gone into space. In the same way, individual selves are gone into the Self.
translator: Working translation for Atman from the Sanskrit, awaiting review
edition: Sanskrit: Āgamaśāstra, ed. V. G. Āpaṭe, Ānandāśrama Sanskrit Series 10 (Pune, 1921), as input on GRETIL
notes: Nothing went anywhere. The lights over the drying board were the same before the pot was made and after it broke; only the pot changed. Gauḍapāda carries the example on through 3.9.
